consensus_summary: Uncircumcision primarily symbolizes the unregenerate sinful nature or flesh, a closed stubborn heart unresponsive to God, and alienation from covenant; removal signifies spiritual cleansing and consecration (heart-circumcision by the Spirit).
book_summary: The foreskin is the blocking flesh (“the body of the sins of the flesh”) covering a covenant member and stopping its work (heart cannot humble/love, ear cannot hearken, lips cannot be heard, fruit forbidden until the year); cut it away or be cut off.
consensus_core_identification: sinful/unregenerate flesh or hardness of heart requiring removal for covenant faithfulness
book_core_identification: blocking flesh (body of the sins of the flesh) covering and impeding the work of a covenant member
boundary_disagreement: Book narrows primary force to functional blockage of faculties/produce of covenant members and does not treat pure ethnic-outsider labels (e.g., Philistines/Gentiles) as central symbolic cases, while consensus primary + common alternatives include broader outsider status and general unregeneracy.
rationale: Both cores identify the foreskin with the sinful flesh that must be put off (book’s explicit Col 2:11 decode matches consensus primary). Book preserves that referent but materially refines precision and extension by defining it as a covering that stops the work of covenant members and by centering the functional examples (heart/ear/lips/fruit) drawn from the shared texts, thereby narrowing the cases relative to consensus breadth without replacing the central category.
strongest_objection: Consensus commonly elevates ethnic/covenantal outsider status as a primary or co-equal sense; the book’s insistence on covering ‘a covenant member’ could be read as excluding rather than merely refining that range of cases.
